description: Films with a replacement cost equal to 20.99 are included along with those above it.

a.request: Among films whose replacement cost is at least 20.99, compute for each rating the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values). Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded).
a.sql:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean
  FROM per_rating
)
SELECT p.rating,
       p.avg_ratio,
       p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS diff_above_mean
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL
  AND p.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
  AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean;

b.request: For each rating, compute the average of rental_rate / rental_duration over films with replacement_cost >= 20.99 (NULLs ignored), then take the unweighted mean of those per-rating averages (NULL averages ignored), and list each rating whose average is strictly greater than that mean, showing the rating, its average, and its unrounded difference from the overall mean.
b.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS overall_mean FROM per_rating) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_rate_per_day AS avg_value, p.avg_rate_per_day - o.overall_mean AS diff_from_mean FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_rate_per_day > o.overall_mean;
b.raw: For each rating, compute the average of rental_rate / rental_duration over films with replacement_cost >= 20.99 (NULLs ignored), then take the unweighted mean of those per-rating averages (NULL averages ignored), and list each rating whose average is strictly greater than that mean, showing the rating, its average, and its unrounded difference from the overall mean.

d.request: For films with `replacement_cost >= 20.99`, compute each rating's average of `rental_rate / rental_duration` (NULLs ignored), take the unweighted mean of those per-rating averages (NULLs ignored), and list each rating whose average is strictly greater than that mean, with its average and its unrounded excess over the mean.
d.sql:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day
  FROM film
  WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99
  GROUP BY rating
),
mean_of_avgs AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS grand_mean
  FROM per_rating
)
SELECT p.rating,
       p.avg_rate_per_day,
       p.avg_rate_per_day - m.grand_mean AS excess_over_mean
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN mean_of_avgs m
WHERE p.avg_rate_per_day > m.grand_mean;

c.request: Using 20.99 as the replacement-cost cutoff for films, compute for each rating the average of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` over the qualifying films (ignoring missing values). Then take the simple mean of these per-rating averages, ignoring missing ones. If that overall mean exists, list each rating whose average is strictly greater than it, showing the rating, its average, and how far its average is above the overall mean (all unrounded). Films with a replacement cost equal to 20.99 are included along with those above it.
c.sql: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio FROM film WHERE replacement_cost >= 20.99 GROUP BY rating), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_mean FROM per_rating WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_ratio, p.avg_ratio - o.overall_mean AS diff_above_mean FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE o.overall_mean IS NOT NULL AND p.avg_ratio IS NOT NULL AND p.avg_ratio > o.overall_mean ORDER BY p.rating;
